title: Regular sequences over polynomial rings and their degree-one syzygies
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $s\ge1$, $m\ge0$, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ be a regular sequence in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Put $S=R[z_1,\ldots,z_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and regard the $f_i$ as constant polynomials. Then $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ is regular in $S$. Moreover, in the free module $S^s$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module] of $s$-tuples with standard unit vectors $e_i$, every $v=(v_1,\ldots,v_s)$ satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^s f_iv_i=0$ admits coefficients $b_{ij}\in S$ such that $$v=\sum_{1\le i<j\le s}b_{ij}(f_ie_j-f_je_i).$$

source.place: Tag 0BIQ (lemma-blowup-regular-sequence), polynomial-extension H_1 argument, specialized to regular sequences; Tag 062F (lemma-regular-koszul-regular) and Tags 0622/0623 (definition-koszul, definition-koszul-complex), explicit differential.

proof.text: Put S = MvPolynomial (Fin m) R, using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Regularity [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] implies R is nontrivial. The monomial basis makes S a nontrivial free R-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module], hence faithfully flat. Apply Mathlib RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular.of_faithfullyFlat and List.map_ofFn to obtain regularity of the sequence of constant polynomials in S. This replaces the longer coefficientwise proof of the same polynomial-extension step.
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] to the regular sequence in S. By [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], degree-one homology of its Koszul complex is zero.

For any commutative ring A and finite sequence f, identify the degree-zero and degree-one terms of [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] using exteriorPower.zeroEquiv and exteriorPower.oneEquiv and identify finite Finsupp vectors with tuples. Prove the coordinate formulas directly from contraction: d_1(v) = sum_i f_i v_i, and d_2(u wedge w) = (sum_i f_i u_i) w - (sum_i f_i w_i) u. The given relation is therefore a degree-one cycle. The exactAt_iff_isZero_homology equivalence for [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] and ShortComplex.moduleCat_exact_iff supply a degree-two preimage w.

Expand the preimage w in the exterior-square basis of [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis], obtained from the standard Finsupp basis. Each basis index is a two-element subset p; its increasing enumeration t_p has t_p(0) < t_p(1). The degree-two differential formula sends that basis vector to f_(t_p(0)) e_(t_p(1)) - f_(t_p(1)) e_(t_p(0)). Define b_ij to be the sum of the coefficients of all p with t_p(0)=i and t_p(1)=j. Commute the finite sums; the two indicator conditions leave exactly the displayed sum over i<j. This works for length zero as well as length one, where the exterior-square basis and the relation sum are empty, so the stated s>=1 hypothesis is not needed by this calculation.

lean.statement: theorem polynomial_regular_sequence_syzygies {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (s m : ℕ) (hs : 1 ≤ s) (f : Fin s → R) (hf : IsRegular R (List.ofFn f)) : IsRegular (R := MvPolynomial (Fin m) R) (MvPolynomial (Fin m) R) (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin s ↦ MvPolynomial.C (f i))) ∧ ∀ v : Fin s → MvPolynomial (Fin m) R, (∑ i : Fin s, MvPolynomial.C (f i) * v i) = 0 → ∃ b : Fin s → Fin s → MvPolynomial (Fin m) R, v = ∑ i : Fin s, ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun j : Fin s ↦ i < j), b i j • (Pi.single j (MvPolynomial.C (f i)) - Pi.single i (MvPolynomial.C (f j)))
